purpose: Sixteenth expanded public source layer focused on reaction-source provenance and evidence-quality strategy: structured reaction database schema, patent and literature extraction, negative or failed-reaction data, procedure and condition metadata, atom mapping and role assignment, natural-product structure revision, process starting-material and impurity-control boundaries, and CASP route benchmark lineage.

promotion_requirements: manual chemist, informatics, process, regulatory, and provenance review

explicit source type, extraction method, schema fields, procedure metadata, atom mapping, negative-data context, structural-assignment evidence, process-control rationale, or benchmark manifest before proposal promotion
separate database-schema, patent/literature-extraction, negative-data, procedure-metadata, atom-map, natural-product-structure, process-control, and benchmark-lineage policy

route-specific provenance, license, curation status, extraction confidence, role assignment, stereochemical evidence, impurity purge logic, starting-material justification, route feasibility, and benchmark split review
legal, patent, regulatory, hazardous-procedure, genotoxic-impurity, natural-product-bioactivity, data-license, or reproducibility review where relevant
safety_scope: records intentionally avoid procedural quantities, operating conditions, and implementation protocols
v17 records are source-quality and provenance priors only and must not auto-close routes as stock, validated procedures, confirmed patents, or regulatory-ready control strategies

families.name: Structured reaction database schema, identifiers, provenance, and license boundaries
families.strategic_principle: Separate a reaction record from its source schema, curator, license, identifiers, and missing metadata. A database hit is a source candidate, not a validated route, unless provenance and fields support the planning claim.

families.name: Patent, journal, figure, and text-mined reaction extraction boundaries
families.strategic_principle: Separate chemistry precedent from extraction artifacts. Patent or literature-mined records require source section, role assignment, figure/text extraction confidence, and curator review before strategic use.

families.name: Negative, low-yield, failed, and high-throughput reaction outcome data policy
families.strategic_principle: Separate absence of literature success from explicit negative evidence. Failed or low-yield records are valuable route boundaries only when the attempted substrate, conditions class, analytical endpoint, and publication or ELN context are traceable.

families.name: Procedure, action-sequence, reagent-role, condition, workup, and scale metadata completeness
families.strategic_principle: Separate a formal reaction equation from executable procedure context. Missing role labels, order of addition, workup, atmosphere, scale, or analytical endpoint should reduce route trust even when the product/reactant string looks valid.

families.name: Atom mapping, reactant/reagent role assignment, reaction-center, and template-lineage policy
families.strategic_principle: Separate bond-disconnection logic from atom-map and role-assignment confidence. Strategic templates must carry reaction-center lineage and must not trust noisy maps or reagent/product role confusion blindly.

families.name: Natural-product structure revision, stereochemical assignment, and spectral-comparison evidence
families.strategic_principle: Separate target identity from proposed literature structure. Natural-product route records require structural-assignment evidence, spectral comparison, stereochemical provenance, and revision history before using a target as a planning endpoint.

families.name: Process starting-material justification, impurity purge, control-strategy, and regulatory boundary
families.strategic_principle: Separate retrosynthetic convenience from process starting-material acceptance and impurity control. A proposed convergent precursor is not a strategic stock anchor unless material attributes, impurity fate, and control strategy are reviewed.

families.name: CASP route benchmark, gold route, stock set, split, and trace-lineage policy
families.strategic_principle: Separate benchmark success from real route quality. A planner trace must carry stock-set, split, route-source, scorer, and feasibility-review lineage before it is used as strategic training or promotion evidence.

anchors.name: Structured reaction database anchor with reviewed schema, identifiers, source provenance, curation status, and license
Extracted reaction anchor with reviewed patent or literature section, extraction modality, role labels, and curator confidence
Negative or failed-reaction anchor with reviewed attempted substrate, conditions class, endpoint, and data-bias context
Procedure metadata anchor with reviewed action sequence, reagent roles, order, scale, workup, and analytical endpoint
Atom-map and reaction-center anchor with reviewed map confidence, role assignment, reagent separation, and template lineage
Natural-product target anchor with reviewed structure revision, stereochemical assignment, spectral comparison, and biosynthetic plausibility
Process starting-material anchor with reviewed impurity fate, purge, material attributes, and control strategy
Benchmark route anchor with reviewed gold trace, source route, stock set, split, scorer, and feasibility lineage

disconnections.name: Reaction record to structured schema plus source, identifier, license, and missing-field provenance policy

forward_logic: separate a database row from the original experimental source
track identifiers, curator, license, schema version, and missing fields
flag records where source provenance or role fields are insufficient for route promotion
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward structured database records only when schema version, source, license, and missing-field status are explicit.

evidence.citation: The Open Reaction Database describes a schema and infrastructure for structuring and sharing organic reaction data.
The ORD schema documentation exposes structured reaction metadata fields including provenance and identifiers.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit schema version, identifiers, source, license, curator, and missing-field status

disconnections.name: Structured reaction corpus to missing metadata, role ambiguity, and dataset-boundary policy

break_bonds: merged dataset to row-level provenance boundary
schema completeness to route trust boundary
forward_logic: separate harmonized datasets from row-level evidence
track missing conditions, missing yields, duplicate rows, and source conflicts
avoid ranking a route highly because it appears in a corpus without completeness checks
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use missing-metadata policy when a reaction exists in a corpus but lacks the fields needed for route trust.

evidence.citation: A call for public open reaction databases motivates structured reporting of chemical reactions.
ORDerly discusses datasets and benchmarks for chemical reaction data derived from structured sources.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit row completeness, duplicates, source conflicts, and provenance manifest

disconnections.name: Extracted patent reaction to source section, claim/example context, and artifact policy

break_bonds: extracted event to source text boundary
forward_logic: separate patent disclosure from experimentally reliable precedent
track whether the reaction came from an example, claim, table, or automatically extracted text
flag patents where role labels, yields, analytical endpoints, or actual examples are unclear
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward patent-derived sources only when example context and extraction confidence are explicit.

risks: patent legal scope confused with feasibility

evidence.citation: Patent reaction event extraction work describes named-entity and event extraction for chemical reactions in patents.
Patent chemical-recognition analysis discusses the difficulty of extracting chemical information from patents.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit patent section, example status, extraction confidence, yield, and analytical endpoint

disconnections.name: Journal figure or text-mined reaction to OCR, diagram, condition, and role-linking policy

forward_logic: separate visually extracted reaction arrows and labels from curated chemistry
track segmentation, OCR, structure recognition, arrow direction, and condition linking
require manual review when a route card comes from a scheme image
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use extraction-boundary records when the source came from a figure or mined text rather than a curated reaction table.

evidence.citation: ReactionDataExtractor reports automated extraction of information from chemical reaction schemes.
Automated chemical reaction extraction from scientific literature frames extraction as product extraction plus role labeling.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit extraction modality, OCR/OSR confidence, step segmentation, and curator review

disconnections.name: Blocked disconnection to explicit failed or low-yield reaction evidence plus bias-context policy

break_bonds: literature absence to explicit negative-evidence boundary
forward_logic: separate unreported reactions from traceable failed experiments
track substrate, condition class, endpoint, analytical method, and reason for failure if known
penalize route branches only when negative data maps to the same substrate or close analogues
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use negative data to down-rank a disconnection only when attempted substrate and endpoint metadata are explicit.

evidence.citation: Machine-learning reactivity study emphasizes the importance of failed experiments and negative examples.
Negative-data perspective discusses negative data in datasets for machine-learning training.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: negative for close analogue failures with explicit endpoint, moderate positive for transparent scope-boundary evidence

disconnections.name: HTE outcome matrix to substrate, condition, success/failure, and robustness-boundary policy

forward_logic: separate an HTE hit from a robust route claim
track reaction matrix design, replicates, controls, success thresholds, and analytical readout
prefer routes whose HTE context includes both positives and negatives across related substrates
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward HTE evidence when outcome matrices expose both productive and unproductive regions.

evidence.citation: HTE plus Bayesian deep-learning study discusses feasibility and robustness prediction with high-throughput data.
High-throughput synthesis study uses reaction attempts to predict reaction success and synthesizability.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit matrix design, controls, negative labels, endpoint, and uncertainty or robustness estimates

disconnections.name: Reaction equation to action sequence plus procedure metadata completeness policy

break_bonds: reaction SMILES to executable action boundary
reported equation to procedure completeness boundary
forward_logic: separate product/reactant equation from the experimental procedure needed to execute it
track action sequence, reagent roles, order, workup, isolation, and analytical endpoint
penalize routes whose reaction records cannot support condition or execution claims
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward procedure-backed records when action sequence and role metadata are explicit and source-linked.

evidence.citation: Automated extraction of chemical synthesis actions converts procedure text into action sequences.
Procedure-inference study highlights patent procedure extraction and the impact of data-quality issues.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit action sequence, role labels, order, workup, endpoint, and source procedure

disconnections.name: Conditioned reaction to reagent-role, scale, atmosphere, workup, and reproducibility policy

forward_logic: separate named conditions from their operational roles
track catalyst, base, solvent, atmosphere, concentration, scale, workup, and characterization status
flag route proposals where missing procedure metadata is likely to change feasibility
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use metadata completeness as a route-quality feature when feasibility depends on role, scale, or workup details.

evidence.citation: Procedure-prediction study reports that quality issues in patent-extracted procedures limit model potential.
Organic synthesis automation review notes that synthesis is often incompletely documented.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for role-labeled conditions, scale, atmosphere, workup, isolation, and characterization evidence

disconnections.name: Mapped reaction to reaction-center template plus atom-map confidence and lineage policy

forward_logic: separate atom-map output from chemically reviewed disconnection logic
track mapping confidence, changed atoms, balance, stereochemistry, and template extraction method
avoid template promotion when map errors or role ambiguity define the apparent bond change
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward atom-mapped templates only when reaction-center lineage and mapping confidence are explicit.

evidence.citation: RXNMapper work shows attention-guided atom mapping and reaction-grammar extraction from reaction data.
Precise atom-to-atom mapping work frames AAM as important for understanding reaction mechanisms.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit map confidence, reaction center, balance, stereochemistry, and template extractor version

disconnections.name: Reaction record to reactant/reagent/product role assignment plus route-center policy

break_bonds: left-of-arrow molecule list to role-assignment boundary
precursor set to bond-forming participant boundary
forward_logic: separate molecules that contribute atoms from reagents, catalysts, solvents, and bystanders
track role labeling source, atom contribution, and route-center participation
penalize disconnections derived from records where role labels or atom contribution are ambiguous
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use role-assignment records to avoid treating reagents or catalysts as strategic precursors.

risks: solvent or catalyst treated as stock branch

evidence.citation: Automated reaction extraction from literature uses product extraction and reaction role labeling.
ORD schema documentation includes reaction-input metadata useful for source and role provenance.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit atom contribution, role labels, catalyst/solvent separation, and product verification

disconnections.name: Natural-product target to revised structure plus stereochemical and spectral-comparison policy

forward_logic: separate a named natural product from its proposed connectivity and stereochemistry
track revision history, NMR or MS comparison, total synthesis evidence, and biosynthetic plausibility
avoid optimizing routes to a misassigned or unverified target structure
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Require structure-assignment evidence before treating a natural-product target as a fixed endpoint.

evidence.citation: Marine natural-product structure-revision survey emphasizes synthesis and spectroscopy in correcting assignments.
Synthetic studies review highlights structural revisions of marine natural products.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit revision history, spectral match, total synthesis, stereochemical source, and biosynthetic rationale

disconnections.name: Stereochemically ambiguous target to diastereomer set plus assignment-evidence policy

forward_logic: represent unresolved stereochemistry as a target set until evidence fixes the endpoint
track synthesized diastereomers, analytical comparison, and assignment logic
penalize routes that optimize an arbitrary stereoisomer without assignment support
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use stereochemical-assignment records when target identity depends on comparing candidate stereoisomers.

evidence.citation: Streptide synthesis paper reports stereochemical reassignment by preparing and comparing diastereomers.
Ushikulide A synthesis paper reports full stereostructure determination by total synthesis.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit stereoisomer set, comparator synthesis, analytical match, and assignment provenance

disconnections.name: Advanced precursor to process starting-material justification plus non-stock boundary policy

forward_logic: separate planner convenience from process-acceptable starting material status
track supplier/source, synthetic accessibility, impurity fate, purge, and regulatory rationale
avoid route closure on advanced intermediates without explicit process anchor evidence
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Do not treat an advanced precursor as stock unless starting-material justification and impurity-control evidence are explicit.

evidence.citation: ICH Q11 provides guidance on development and manufacture of drug substances and process control concepts.
EMA Q11 page describes the guideline for development and manufacture of drug substances.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit starting-material justification, supplier evidence, impurity profile, purge, and control strategy

disconnections.name: Process route to impurity formation, purge, material attributes, and control-strategy policy

forward_logic: separate chemical feasibility from impurity formation and purge evidence
track genotoxic or carryover impurity risk, purge points, analytical controls, and process parameters
down-rank routes whose strategic precursor creates uncontrolled impurity liabilities
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use impurity-control records when starting material or route choice changes impurity fate.

evidence.citation: ICH Q11 includes examples and concepts for control strategies and impurity control in drug substance manufacture.
EMA Q11 page describes the guideline for development and manufacture of drug substances.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit impurity formation, purge evidence, analytical controls, material attributes, and process parameters

disconnections.name: Benchmark route to gold trace, route source, stock set, split, and leakage-audit policy

forward_logic: separate solved benchmark traces from evidence of practical route quality
track source route, stock set, train/test split, model version, search budget, and leakage audit
avoid using benchmark closure as strategic proof when stock or split artifacts explain success
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward benchmark-derived sources only when route lineage, stock set, split, and leakage status are explicit.

evidence.citation: Computer-assisted synthetic planning review describes CASP foundations and route-planning challenges.
AiZynthFinder paper describes open-source retrosynthesis planning software using MCTS and neural networks.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit source route, stock set, split, search budget, model version, and leakage audit

disconnections.name: Planner-generated trace to feasibility review, scorer, route diversity, and human-evidence policy

forward_logic: separate model score from chemist-reviewed feasibility
track scorer version, route diversity, source support, stock policy, and human review labels
avoid reinforcing planner artifacts as strategic source records without independent evidence
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use planner traces as weak evidence unless scorer lineage and human feasibility review are present.

evidence.citation: Retrosynthetic crosstalk study evaluates combinations of planning algorithms and single-step models across practical metrics.
ASKCOS conspectus summarizes open-source data-driven synthesis planning and associated model infrastructure.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit scorer version, source support, route diversity, stock policy, and human review

source_notes.summary: The v17 expansion promotes source-provenance and evidence-quality families covering database schema, extraction confidence, negative data, procedure metadata, atom mapping, structure revision, process control, and benchmark lineage.

V17 records are advisory. Promotion requires provenance, curation, source/license, procedure, mapping, structure-assignment, process-control, or benchmark-lineage evidence; extracted records, patents, planner traces, and database hits must not be treated as validated routes by default.
